after: ## What is the difference between formal and informal education?
alt: Formal and informal education compared on five points. Formal education happens in schools, colleges and universities, follows a planned curriculum, is taught by trained teachers and is assessed by tests. Informal education happens anywhere, is unplanned, is learned from parents, elders, peers and media, and is not formally assessed.
caption: Schooling is only the formal part of education; much learning happens informally.

after: ## What are the official and hidden curricula?
alt: An iceberg. Above the water is the official curriculum: subjects, syllabus content and testing. Below the water, and much larger, is the hidden curriculum: norms and values, punctuality, conformity and gender roles, learned from bells, registers, uniforms, rules and expectations.
caption: Pupils learn far more from how school is organised than from the subjects on the timetable.

after: ## What are the official and hidden curricula?
alt: The hidden curriculum of bells, uniforms, rules and rewards is read in two ways. Functionalists see it as socialising pupils into shared values. Marxists Bowles and Gintis (1976) see it as preparing obedient workers for capitalism.
caption: Functionalists and Marxists agree the hidden curriculum exists but disagree about whom it serves.

after: ## How effective are different types of school?
alt: Four measures of school effectiveness: examination results, social mobility, values and equality of opportunity. Private schools often get higher exam results, though their pupils start with more advantages, but their fees exclude poorer families and may widen inequality.
caption: A school’s effectiveness changes with the measure you choose.

after: ## What alternative approaches to education exist?
alt: A line from adults deciding to the child deciding what is learned: conventional school, homeschooling, progressive schooling such as Summerhill, and unschooling. Below, online learning and vocational learning are summarised with a strength and a limitation each.
caption: Alternative approaches differ most in how much the child controls their own learning.

after: ## How does 5.1 connect to the rest of the Education topic?
alt: Two links. The hidden curriculum from 5.1 is central to functionalist and Marxist views of the roles of education in 5.2. Private and selective schools from 5.1 are part of explanations of class differences in achievement in 5.3.
caption: Learn 5.1 well: its ideas come back in 5.2 and 5.3.
